utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has about two matters to deal with. The first one is about the depositions that were recorded in Belgrade. The Trial Chamber has decided to admit all the depositions recorded in Belgrade into evidence and the depositions are also released to the public subject to the redaction of any names of protected witnesses. The Trial Chamber has observed that most of the objections recorded go to the weight to be attached to the evidence. Otherwise, the Trial Chamber is able to distinguish facts from opinion and also able to disregard matters that are not relevant. On the motion by the Prosecution to call Mr. Marko Tubakovic who was one of the deponents in Belgrade, the Trial Chamber would like to ask Mr. Pisarevic, counsel for Mr. Simo Zaric, who had called him, whether he has any submissions to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. At the time when we proposed this witness, we did that because we wanted him to give evidence regard to a certain event. And I do not know what is it that Mr. Tubakovic knows exactly. In principle, we do not object to calling Mr. Tubakovic so that he could be heard here as a witness but we need to let him know about this but I'll do that when I go to Bosanski Samac one of these days. Well, that is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The Trial Chamber has decided to grant the motion to call Mr. Marko Tubakovic because it considers him an important witness in view of some of the matters he was able to discuss and that it is in the interests of justice to call him to adduce additional evidence in this respect. Therefore, Mr. Pisarevic, as counsel for Mr. Simo Zaric, whose witness Mr. Marko Tubakovic is, you are ordered to call the witness as early as possible once the trial resumes, because he is listed as Mr. Simo Zaric's witness and in keeping with Mr. Simo Zaric's wishes, this witness should be heard before Mr. Simo Zaric testifies. And he has to be heard in his presence. So the Trial Chamber will appreciate it if you can make it -- the arrangements as quickly as possible so that he is able to be heard soon after our proceedings resume on the 28th of April. There are no other matters for the Trial Chamber to deal with at the moment. We shall therefore adjourn -- oh, I see counsel on their feet. Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My learned friend was quicker than me so I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was in the relation to the tender of three outstanding matters we have already flagged. The first is the English translation of P173, that's the document I put into evidence during the evidence of Mr. Omeranovic. I have the English translation here, if it's an appropriate time to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we just reconfirm the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P173. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, are there any other?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. There is also some Red Cross, the ICRC documents that I have provided to my learned friends several weeks ago. They were in response to the Defence of Mr. Tadic tendering several documents from the ICRC relating to prisoner exchange agreements. One of the documents Mr. Lukic was objecting to so I'm not pressing that at the moment. I understand there is no objection from counsel to the other four documents which are the agreements between the parties brokered by the ICRC in relation to the conduct of hostilities and the exchange of prisoners during the indictment period. If there is no objection I tender the following documents. Firstly an agreement between the President of Bosnia, that's Mr. Izetbegovic, the SDS, the SDA, the HDZ and the SDP, with the abbreviations, dated the 22nd of May, 1992, made in Geneva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Secondly is an agreement between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we deal with them one by one so that we number them until complete?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, that one is headed: "Agreement at the invitation of the International Committee of the Red Cross relating to the 22nd of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P176.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the next one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one is titled: "Agreement number 3," it's dated the 6th of June, 1992, and it's called Bosnia-Herzegovina, ICRC plan of action, an agreement between Mr. Izetbegovic's representative, Mr. Karadzic's representative, Mr. Kalinic, a representative of the Croatian Democratic Community, and liaison officer of the Croatian Democratic Community. I tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the next one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Next one is headed: "Agreement on the release and transfer of prisoners," it's dated the 1st of October, 1992, relating to an agreement signed in Geneva on the 30th of September -- sorry an agreement negotiated in Geneva on the 30th of September and 1st of October, 1992, between a representative of Mr. Izetbegovic as president of Bosnia; Mr. Kalinic, as representative of Mr. Karadzic of the Serbian Democratic Party; Mr. Coric, as a representative of Mr. Boban of the Croatian Democratic Community; Mr. Kurjak, as a representative of the Party of Democratic Action, Mr. Popadic, as liaison officer of the Serbian Democratic Party and Mr. Mujic, as liaison officer of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia. I tender that document into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think that last one is sometimes referred to as the Geneva agreement of the 1st of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The final Red Cross document or ICRC document is entitled: "Guidelines on the exchange of prisoners made in Zagreb on the 24th of March, 1993." I tender that one into document as well -- sorry, into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P179.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Finally the third tender or category is, I think, last week, I moved the admission into evidence of Mr. Zaric's book, I informed Chamber's legal officer that we were no longer pressing the tender at that point. We no longer press the tender of the entire book into evidence but I move for the admission of the extracts which have been referred to in evidence to date in relation to the transfer of the prisoners to Brcko on the 26th of April, 1992, that is at pages 243 to 246 of the book in its original edition, and the English translation at pages 175 to 178, and I move to tender into evidence those extracts from the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pisarevic? Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We object to the tender of documents in this manner, in the view of the Defence these are fragments which may not be viewed or taken out of the context of the book as a whole. If the Prosecutor's Office wishes to tender the book into evidence, we shall object to that as well, for the simple reason that Mr. Zaric had -- gave his statement and the Chamber has already been informed that Mr. Zaric will be called to testify before this Chamber, and I therefore think that this book and fragments from it in particular may not constitute evidence or exhibit in this case before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the same issue, can I address the Chamber respectfully?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic, we support the request of the Prosecution with regard to the admission of the evidence, actually the extract of the book or book in its entirety on the following basis: It is not a personal note of defendant Zaric. It is not his personal diary. It is not a personal document. It is a book published, so it is in possession of the everyone who can buy this book. It's same category as all other books and sources relevant to these proceedings, such as commentary on Geneva Conventions, history in Bosnia, et cetera, et cetera. It's simply a book which is accessible to all parties and in the interest of justice we think that it might help this Trial Chamber. Whether in form of extracts of the book, depending on the position of the parties or their strategy, or in its entirety. So we firmly oppose the position of Defence of Mr. Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours may I briefly address on the evidentiary basis for the tender which is simply this: Mr. Zaric's own counsel first referred to that extract in -- I'm sorry, Mr. Pantelic for Mr. Simic first referred to that particular extract in cross-examining Mr. Simeunovic who is mentioned not in that extract but -- I can't recall at the moment, I won't go into that. He mentioned it. Mr. Zaric's own counsel, Mr. Lazarevic, then put to Mr. Simeunovic passages from the book, read passages from the book in his re-examination of Mr. Simeunovic. I referred to passages of the book, read passages, from that very same extract within those pages to the witness, Mr. Topolovac without objection from counsel for Mr. Zaric. I also yesterday referred or two days ago referred to the same passages without reading them because of time considerations of Colonel Nikolic, again without objection in relation to the veracity -- or in relation to the reliability of the account. It's an account of an accused, Mr. Zaric, published after he'd given his three statements and as Mr. Pantelic correctly says, available to the world. If the parties are going to refer to extracts, either paraphrasing or reading them, those portions should be before the Trial Chamber so the Trial Chamber can assess the totality of the extracts in their context. Otherwise, it's just parties reading or quoting, and to date I stress there has been no objection to that course which was in fact begun by Mr. Zaric's own counsel. The Prosecution at the moment isn't pressing the tender of the whole book. If that becomes an issue -- it may become an issue during Mr. Zaric's own testimony. We don't push that at the moment. Only the parts referred to, which in the Prosecution's submission are relevant to evidence given and probative as a version of which witnesses have been asked to comment upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber will grant the Prosecution submission and admit the extracts referred to by the Prosecution in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P180 and P180 ter, exhibits, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I merely wish to inform the Trial Chamber that our demographic experts have gone through the material as granted by the decision of this Trial Chamber but yesterday, the programme and the method were not copied. It will be done today in the course of this day so that the disc with this copy will be as the Prosecutor's Office has informed us, will be delivered to the Registry today, later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and this is the very last issue that I would like to address. The Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic was informed two days before by the Defence of Mr. Krajisnik that the position of Defence of Mr. Krajisnik is that Mr. Krajisnik will not be -- give evidence here in form of 92 bis statement or in any other form, because it might affect his position as a defendant in the other case before this Tribunal. So that's the final position after all these months of negotiation and contacts between two defence teams with regard to the testimony of Mr. Krajisnik. So I respectfully ask this Trial Chamber, in the interest of justice, to grant another witness for Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic instead of Mr. Krajisnik, and I will tell you which person is that. It is Dr. Stanko Pivasevic, one of the founders of the SDS branch in Samac in years 1990, and then he was a president of SDS branch in Samac during all these years, presently he's president of the SDS. The summary of his testimony will cover work of SDS in Samac, activities, and details of the acts of the accused, Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Between which periods?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Between October, 1991 and December, 1993. We think that it's relevant to the defence of Mr. Blagoje Simic since during the Defence case specifically during the Defence case of Mr. Simo Zaric, many issues were raised specifically in cross-examination of Prosecution -- of Prosecutor's cross-examination of Mr. Zaric's witnesses, and specifically the role of SDS politics, issues, discussions, et cetera. What I can tell to this Trial Chamber that -- well, don't take me formally stick to this fact but don't think that maybe one hour or hour and a half of testimony of viva voce before this Trial Chamber will be necessary for this particular witness, but as I said, I will prepare a summary, check on the field whether he's available and he can be very, very soon be present in The Hague, even after the -- after the -- our present adjournment. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, there is no objection to this application on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber wishes to make one observation, Mr. Pantelic, that whereas Mr. Krajisnik was going to be limited to discussing the variant A and B, this witness, whom you intend to call in his place, appears to be actually expanding the areas which he's going to discuss before the Trial Chamber. So the Trial Chamber would like to point out that -- make sure that the summary you're going to present in writing is as brief as possible, to cover only the salient features of the defence of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And that is important for the Prosecution to be able to prepare for their cross-examination, and when -- so that when you call him you don't go outside the summary that you provide.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I am very grateful to your instructions. Among other things he will give testimony of variant A and B, whether it was in discussion or not, whether this existed or not within the scope of activities of the SDS in Samac and also the other short topics, and I will do as soon as possible this summary and I will forward it to the Prosecution. It will be very brief, I can assure you, his presence here. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So can the Prosecution expect the summary before the end of today?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe that we can do that. Just a moment, can I have just a second to confer with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go. You can approach him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I have -- if I will have situation for ten minutes to confer with my client after the adjournment, then I will get the proofing notes from him and then I will type it immediately in the Defence counsel room and I will forward it today, this morning, to Prosecution. If it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you will be allowed to have the time you need before the accused is taken back to the detention unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, in that regard the Prosecution would appreciate it if Mr. Pantelic could provide us with the full name, full accurate name of this witness, and if possible his date of birth and if that's not possible today, as soon as possible thereafterwards and then of course any other well known nicknames of this particular individual. So that's important to us to be able to research him. If Your Honours please there is just one other matter that I want to raise and that's the issue of sequence of witnesses upon our resumption on the 28th of April and related to that is your order that Mitar Mitrovic appear here on the Monday the 28th of April at 9.00 a.m.. What -- may I ask what sequence of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Actually the time was rescheduled to the afternoon of the 28th. The latest calendar we are starting at 14.15. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well, on our resumption on the 28th in the afternoon, I take it the Chamber anticipates that he will be the first witness. We need to know this so that we can of course prepare our cross-examinations and apportion subsequent witnesses amongst ourselves, for a start. And secondly, if Your Honour pleases, may I will also ask what procedure you actually envisage for this man? I take it -- am I correct that the Chamber will question him and that he will then be open to cross-examination by the parties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That will be the procedure. The Chamber will examine him and then the Defence counsels will be given an opportunity to cross-examine him and then the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On the sequence of witnesses, Mr. Di Fazio, at the moment it's not possible to decide specifically because of the health of Mr. Simo Zaric. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you. If Your Honours please, I wonder if there is some way that we might be able to resolve the matter before we resume on the 28th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The legal officer will keep in touch because the Trial Chamber is monitoring the health of Mr. Simo Zaric. So depending on whether or not he will be able to attend the proceedings, the Trial Chamber will be able to say which witnesses will come, the sequence of witnesses. But it is important for the Prosecution is to know the available witnesses and just prepare for all of them. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Mr. Pantelic at least can, I think, provide us with his intended sequence of witnesses and if he does that, that would also be a very -- of considerable assistance to the Prosecution and to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That will be subject to their ability to get visas and to travel and also there is one witness for Mr. Blagoje Simic whom Mr. Simo Zaric wanted to be -- to hear, to be present. So all those points must be taken into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is one matter which I wish to raise. It was in relation to the motion filed on the 11th of April by the Prosecution in relation to the calling of Marko Tubakovic which Your Honours granted this morning. We filed it confidentially only because the testimony was given in closed session and had not been admitted. There was no other reason we filed it confidentially. Perhaps the Trial Chamber would like to look at the motion and if -- and assess whether it should remain confidential. I don't -- I'm not saying on the spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the Trial Chamber has already released the -- all the depositions to the public, the only reason it was in closed session was because of the security concerns at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I only filed it because it had closed session written all over the top of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that is understandable so there is no reason for it to be -- continue to be in closed session, I mean to be filed confidentially so the confidentiality is lifted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There being no other business, the Trial Chamber will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 9.39 a.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 28th day of April, 2003, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
